sections.title: Oncology Nursing: Assessment, Diagnosis, & Cancer Management
sections.description: This course utilizes a clinical framework to explore commonly encountered cancers. Students critically examine specific cancers with respect to prevention and screening, diagnosis and staging, evidence-based treatment, and follow-up care. Students systematically analyze clinical data and contemporary evidence to diagnose and manage cancer related symptoms and complications of cancer therapies. Clinical scenarios are employed within the context of complex histories, sociocultural influences, and age and gender specific variations to develop individualized cancer management plans. Political, economic, and social issues as applicable to cancer care are also explored.

sections.title: Oncology Nursing: Assessment, Diagnosis, & Cancer Management
sections.description: Emphasis is on the application of critical thinking and diagnostic reasoning skills in advanced clinical decision making. Students access, diagnose, and manage the care of oncology patients with a variety of cancers. The delivery of care and evaluation of role effectiveness within the health care system are examined. Online course with both synchronous and asynchronous components. Course includes 240 clinical hours in an oncology setting
